bullets.title: Global chip selloff deepens: semis down 3-5% amid AI capex ROI doubts and China DUV threat
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks extended losses globally with the iShares Semi ETF (SOXX) down ~3.7% premarket; MU -6.2%, STX -7.1%, WDC/SNDK -7%, AMD -4.4%, NVDA credit spreads spiking. Dual catalysts: China's DUV lithography progress stoking competitive fears (though analysts note ASML's 2008-era tech only reaches 28nm single-shot, requiring multi-patterning for 7nm) and mounting skepticism over AI capex ROI with hyperscaler FCF turning negative.

bullets.title: KOSPI crashes 10.8%, 2nd biggest drop on record; Korea AI bubble unwinding triggers global contagion
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI halted twice after crashing 10.8% — its 2nd largest single-day drop on record — as leveraged ETF margin calls cascaded (AUM halved from $53B to $27B). The index is now down 34% from June highs after a 297% bull run since April 2025, with 25% of sessions since June 1 closing down 5%+. SK Hynix fell 14.7%, Samsung 13.4%; the KOSPI now trades at a record-low 5.1x forward PE.

bullets.title: AI circular-finance narrative spooks credit markets; hyperscaler CDS hits record wides
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks (22V, MS, Jefferies) flagged a growing concern: NVDA's $250B OpenAI DC financing and $50B HUT Texas lease deals create circular dependency where hyperscaler capex funds NVDA chip purchases. Hyperscaler CDS spreads hit new record wides; META's $12.5B data center bond priced near junk-level rates (+25bps wider YTD). MS credit analysts see no systemic funding problem given NVDA's balance sheet strength, but market is treating it as distress signal.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley maintains AI bull case: 25-50% ROIC for hyperscalers; momentum selloff at dotcom-era volatility
bullets.body: MS's Brian Nowak models 25-50% ROIC for hyperscalers owning both models and infrastructure (GOOGL ~46%, AMZN/MSFT/META ~25-30%). US TMT momentum has reversed its entire 20%+ bounce and dropped 40% from June highs — volatility at levels only seen in dotcom unwind, GFC, and post-COVID boom. SOX trades at 15.8x 2Y forward PE, 8% discount to SPX (widest since Oct 2022). MS stays bullish: compute demand to exceed supply for years constrained by power, memory, packaging.

bullets.title: JPMorgan turns bullish on stocks broadly; Fed hike probability priced ~33-40%
bullets.body: JPMorgan officially shifted to a bullish equity stance. Separately, Citadel Securities expects the Fed to raise rates this week; market pricing implies 33-40% probability of a hike per multiple sources. Internal Fed dissent is elevated with Waller publicly challenging Warsh, suggesting 3-6 dissenters on next decision. JPM research itself labels the meeting a 'hawkish hold.'

bullets.title: 2Q GDP tracking ~2% with solid 3% domestic demand; trade drags ~1ppt on import reversal
bullets.body: PSC Macro and Morgan Stanley both tracking 2Q real GDP at ~2%, with trade/inventories subtracting ~1ppt after a broad-based decline in imports (reversing May front-loading). Private domestic final demand tracks ~2.7-3% supported by AI-driven capex. Tariff refunds now exceed tariff payments; effective tariff rate below 7% and falling. Richmond Fed ISM-equivalent at 53.3-58.2%, pointing to July ISM upside vs 54.0% consensus.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence softens to 90.8; lower-income cohort hit hardest by Iran War gas prices
bullets.body: Conference Board consumer confidence fell 1.4pts to 90.8 in July, with the Present Situation Index hitting a cycle low of 114.9 (-3.6pts). The <$15K income cohort sits at 63.4 confidence. Contrarily, BofA card data shows lower-income spending growth now outpacing higher-income for the first time (K-shape ending), supported by stronger labor income and lower fuel costs.

bullets.title: Tech sector down 12% from peak in 56 days — historically shallow vs. median 25.7% / 73-day correction
bullets.body: The tech sector is down 12% from its peak over 56 days. Historically, the median tech selloff drops 25.7% and bottoms in 73 days; current drawdown is one of the shallowest on record. All historical tech drawdowns have recovered to new all-time highs.

bullets.title: Dealer gamma collapsed to zero; short gamma regime dominates with -$14B/1% SPX exposure
bullets.body: MS QDS flags dealer option gamma at zero with levered ETF short gamma now dominating. Global short gamma estimated at -$14bn per 1% SPX move. Macro systematic strategies hold no stock to sell currently but at 70th percentile leverage — will be material sellers on 2%+ down days. Hedge funds saw largest single-day degrossing since April; nets at 35th percentile but grosses still elevated at 85th percentile.

bullets.title: META and BlackRock announce $14B, 1-GW Texas data center campus targeting 2028 launch
bullets.body: META and BlackRock are establishing a joint venture to develop a ~$14B, 1-gigawatt data center campus in El Paso, Texas, expected online by 2028. META separately priced a $12.5B debt offering Monday at higher rates than comparable prior-year deals, underscoring rising cost of AI capex financing.

bullets.title: MSFT F4Q26 preview: Street expects $87.6B revenue, 40.3% Azure growth; capex guidance key watch
bullets.body: MSFT reports F4Q26 with Street at $87.62B revenue (above $87.25B guide midpoint) and 40.3% Azure cc growth with buy-side expecting higher. EPS consensus $4.63. Key focus: capex guidance ($189B FY27 consensus), M365 Copilot monetization details, and open-source AI strategy signal. Amazon separately is winding down most flagship in-house AI models, pivoting strategy.

bullets.title: Jefferies: AI trade unwind driven by narrative/positioning, not fundamentals; no clear re-entry catalyst near-term
bullets.body: Jefferies flags tech momentum down 50% in recent stretch with the best and worst 30-day returns both occurring in the last 2 months. Key concerns: frontier lab business model durability, open-weight competition, capex funded via debt/equity raises, and CSP credit spreads blowing out. No consensus catalyst to exit digestion phase over the next 2-3 weeks of earnings; post-GOOGL capex confirmation no longer seen as bullish.

bullets.title: Internet sector fell 6-9% on AI capex debate; AMZN, GOOGL, META each -8% with 2027 valuations compressed
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes internet names fell ~7% overall (SPX -1%, NDX -2%), with META/GOOGL both -8%, AMZN -6%, UBER -9%, APP -8%. Multiples: AMZN 20x, GOOGL 21x, META 18x 2027 EPS — down 12-25% vs trailing twelve-month averages. MS marks sector as 'Attractive.'

bullets.title: NVDA takes $5B stake in Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence; in talks to guarantee OpenAI financing
bullets.body: NVDA announced a $5B stake in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence and is reportedly in talks to guarantee financing for OpenAI's data center buildout, deploying its balance sheet to anchor the AI infrastructure ecosystem. Jim Cramer separately stated he will not sell NVDA.

bullets.title: Brent crude falls 3.5% to $85 on US-Iran pause; oil 10% above last FOMC meeting level
bullets.body: Brent crude declined ~3.5% to $85 on hopes of a Strait of Hormuz reopening after a US-Iran pause. Despite today's pullback, oil prices remain approximately 10% above levels at the last FOMC meeting, complicating the Fed's inflation calculus. OPEC+ separately indicated it expects to hold 2026 output steady after September.

bullets.title: Retail investor sentiment craters: AAII bullish sentiment -15pts in one week, largest drop in 25 years
bullets.body: JPM notes retail net buying fell to its lowest level since the Covid pandemic; the basket of retail favorites is down 13% in July, the worst month since 2022. AAII bullish sentiment fell more than 15 points in a single week — the largest such drop in 25 years. Semis L/S positioning at 98th percentile remains a structural headwind.

bullets.title: US home prices modestly accelerating; Case-Shiller +1.11% y/y in May, MS targets 2% by year-end
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Case-Shiller National Index accelerated to +1.11% y/y in May from +0.94% in April; FHFA rose +2.24% y/y. Strategists believe home price appreciation has bottomed and expect pickup to ~2% y/y by year-end as inventory growth slows, though affordability remains challenged and lower rates are needed to spark demand.

bullets.title: JPM semis update: SOX gained 87.8% in Q2 (best quarter ever), then fell 20% peak-to-trough; bull case intact
bullets.body: JPM's Global Thematic notes SOX's best-ever quarterly gain of 87.8% in Q2 2026 (INTC, MRVL, MU all +200%), followed by a 20.2% peak-to-trough drawdown June 22-July 17 driven by retail deleveraging and ETF rebalancing. JPM aligns with the bull case: fundamental story intact with ~12% US semis revenue growth and ~23% earnings growth expected YoY. Chinese LLMs now represent ~60% token share used by US firms on OpenRouter at costs as low as $0.02/task vs $2.75 for Claude.

bullets.title: SMCI Taiwan offices raided over alleged NVDA chip smuggling to China; NVDA employee detained
bullets.body: Taiwan prosecutors detained an NVDA employee and raided SMCI's Taiwan offices as part of an investigation into alleged smuggling of NVDA chips to China. This adds regulatory and geopolitical risk to the NVDA/SMCI supply chain narrative.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex accelerating: Google 2027 capex tracking $287B (+45% y/y); compute scarcity benefits neoclouds
bullets.body: Per a liquid cooling/hyperscaler note, Google's 2027 capex is moving toward ~$287B (+$23B, +45% y/y) while MSFT capex expected $40B+ per quarter in 2026. H100 spot index at all-time highs despite new AI infrastructure announcements. Neocloud stocks (ORCL, CRWV, NBIS) down 21-32% since META's July 1 neocloud announcement but may benefit from pricing power and compute scarcity.
